env: Node: process field holding the environment
argv: Node: process field holding the command line
cwd: Node: process method answering the working directory
platform: Node: process field naming the operating system
version: Node: process field holding the runtime version
versions: Node: process field holding the dependency versions
pid: Node: process field holding the process id
ppid: Node: process field holding the parent process id
arch: Node: process field naming the CPU architecture
execPath: Node: process field holding the executable path
execArgv: Node: process field holding the runtime options
nextTick: Node: process method scheduling a callback
setTimeout: Node: global scheduling a delayed callback
setInterval: Node: global scheduling a repeating callback
queueMicrotask: WHATWG HTML: global scheduling a microtask
__dirname: Node: CommonJS module global holding the directory
__filename: Node: CommonJS module global holding the file path
container: suss: deployment target for code running as a plain container
schedule: suss: effect class for a scheduled callback
zod: schema library a program validates its environment with
valibot: schema library a program validates its environment with
envalid: environment validator a program validates its environment with
znv: environment parser a program validates its environment with
parse: zod and valibot: the call that validates a value
safeParse: zod and valibot: parse that returns a result instead of throwing
parseAsync: zod and valibot: the asynchronous form of parse
safeParseAsync: zod and valibot: the asynchronous form of safeParse
optional: zod and valibot: the wrapper that accepts a missing value
nullish: zod: the wrapper that accepts null or a missing value
catch: language: the JavaScript keyword, which zod spells its fallback method the same way as
or: zod: the union that accepts a second schema
cleanEnv: envalid: the call a program parses its environment with
devDefault: envalid: the option supplying a value outside production
parseEnv: znv: the call a program parses its environment with
createEnv: @t3-oss/env-core: the call a program declares its environment with
runtimeEnv: @t3-oss/env-core: the option the environment object goes under
server: @t3-oss/env-core: the schema section for server-side variables
shared: @t3-oss/env-core: the schema section both sides read
properties: suss: a schema reader finds several literals under named keys
builtAt: suss: a schema reader finds an argument that is a builder call
builtAtReceiver: suss: a schema reader finds a receiver that is a builder call
